headline: FSU’s lowest performers from Friday night’s loss, per PFF

paragraphs.text: A lopsided loss usually leaves plenty of blame to go around, and Florida State’s 44-20 defeat at Louisville was no exception. The Seminoles allowed the game to get away from them after building an early two-touchdown lead, with the defense struggling to contain Louisville once the Cardinals found their rhythm.

The final score told the broader story, but Pro Football Focus’ individual grades offered a more specific look at where the performance broke down. Here are Florida State’s five lowest-graded players from the loss to Louisville, according to PFF.
Diggs rounded out the bottom five with a 52.3 overall grade across 19 snaps. His 61.0 pass-rush grade was his strongest category, while PFF graded him at 50.5 against the run and 28.3 as a tackler.

Unlike the two players above him, Jones had a substantial role, playing 49 defensive snaps. His 65.6 run-defense grade was a positive, but a 27.0 tackling grade and 44.5 coverage grade pulled down his overall evaluation.
Knight also saw limited action, appearing for five defensive snaps. He finished with a 45.4 overall grade, while PFF assigned him a 47.6 run-defense grade and 20.4 tackling mark.
Cromartie’s evaluation came from an extremely limited sample, with the safety playing only two defensive snaps. His 44.5 overall grade included a 52.0 run-defense mark and a 20.4 tackling grade.
Anderson received FSU’s lowest overall grade after playing 15 defensive snaps. PFF gave him a 47.5 run-defense grade, 46.5 tackling grade, and 46.7 pass-rush grade.
This article originally appeared on FSU Wire: FSU’s lowest performers from Friday night’s loss, per PFF
